state:
- The free-exposure anchor is likely internally inconsistent and the risk is deferred instead of computed: with >99% protein binding, the candidate's ~70 µg/mL steady-state figure (which itself exceeds typical teriflunomide label means and is admittedly unverified) plus a ~0.4–0.6% free fraction leaves free drug plausibly below even the low end of the stated 0.5–6 µM IC50 range, meaning the central go/no-go gate may fail arithmetic before any live-cell work; fix by pre-computing bounding scenarios (label exposure × measured free fraction × IC50 range) in Step 0 so the exposure-gate risk is quantified up front rather than only promised as a future measurement.
- Prior-art acknowledgment omits the most probable direct precedent: the packet correctly supports DHODH-inhibition-driven differentiation via brequinar (S4), but the candidate's novelty re-scoping only flags brequinar trials and clinical-stage DHODH inhibitors as unverified prior knowledge and never checks for published teriflunomide/leflunomide (A77-1726) work in AML or myeloid differentiation — the exact drug proposed; a targeted Step 0 literature check for teriflunomide or A77-1726 in AML is required before the 'responder-biology stratifier' can credibly stand as the sole novelty claim.
- The flux-defined responder subset, on which novelty now rests, lacks pre-registered validation criteria: no specimen count, assay acceptance/stability rules, or decision threshold for how many independent primary blasts must show baseline DHO:orotate/salvage-capacity correlation with EC50 before the stratifier is real, and no explicit mapping onto the marker-defined CD11b/CD14-low population (which is itself partly defined by the drug's own endpoint, risking circularity); fix by pre-registering a per-specimen sample-size and concordance rule linking metabolic stratification to the immunophenotypic subset.
